sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Villenave-d'Ornon, south-east of Bordeaux, has no paid on-street scheme that we could find. The town's civility page says parking is mostly alternate-side, odd house numbers from the 1st to the 15th of the month and even numbers from the 16th, with some streets fixed to one side by signs [9]. The municipal police page lists obstructive parking among the offences it records and describes no paid-parking or blue-zone scheme, which does not prove there is none [10]. A page of 10 June 2026 says rue René Voisin is to be redeveloped after resident consultation, creating 28 marked spaces on the odd-numbered side, with no start date given [11]. Rue Jean-Pagès is being rebuilt from 6 January 2026 to 26 November 2027, with parking banned beside active works and new parking for cars and lorries in the project [12]. The metropolitan low-emission zone applies inside the ring road, and the Pyrénées park-and-ride is not among the 11 open to unclassified vehicles; the page does not say whether it lies inside the zone [5][6].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big changes are on rails. Bordeaux Métropole said on 9 June 2026 that works on the rail upgrade south of Bordeaux, with a third track and crossing points at four stations including Villenave-d'Ornon, began in 2025, and that four multimodal interchange hubs are planned, one of them here, with service entry planned for 2032 and no figures for station parking [15]. A regional page of September 2024 describes the same programme from December 2024 to 2032, with TER line 44 journeys ten minutes longer in the meantime; it may not reflect the situation now [16]. The town's page announced new tram lines E and F from 6 December 2025 and a simplified line C running to Villenave Pyrénées, with a tram every ten minutes in the daytime, but does not itself confirm that the change took place [14]. The renovated market square in the Chambéry district was due to be inaugurated on 25 March 2026 with 18 marked spaces [17]. Metropolis-wide, charging costs 0.38 euro per kWh with a surcharge after four hours, according to a page of May 2025 that does not show whether it still applies [7], and use of the public network rose 54% in the first quarter of 2025 [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The key site is TBM's Pyrénées park-and-ride at the end of tram C, with 753 spaces, 20 of them with charging points, and a height limit of 1.90 m, open to all [0]. Parking is included in a TBM subscription; others buy a ticket at 4.50 euros, or 3.50 euros at the reduced rate, which includes round trips for up to seven people [1]. TBM's own pages disagree on the closing hours and the fine for cars left outside operating hours, 15 euros on one and 25 on another [2]. Pyrénées is one of 11 sites selling short-stay tickets of 12 to 25 euros for two to five days [3], but not one of the six offering an overnight-near-home subscription of 300 euros a year [4]. A mobile bike shop is based at the site [13].

Our data cover this park-and-ride for 27 days since 24 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 16% on weekdays and 9% at weekends, with a peak of 39% on a Tuesday afternoon. It is a large car park with plenty of room.
